In rectangle $ ABCD$, points $ F$ and $ G$ lie on $ \overline{AB}$ so that $ AF = FG = GB$ and $ E$ is the midpoint of $ \overline{DC}$. Also, $ \overline{AC}$ intersects $ \overline{EF}$ at $ H$ and $ \overline{EG}$ at $ J$. The area of the rectangle $ ABCD$ is $ 70$. Find the area of triangle $ EHJ$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is rectangle ABCD, with A at the lower left, B at the lower right, C at the upper right, and D at the upper left. F and G are on the bottom side AB, trisecting AB; E is at the midpoint of the top side DC. Diagonal AC connects from A to C, segment EF intersects AC at H, and segment EG intersects AC at J. Then reason: Let the rectangle coordinates be A=(0,0), B=(w,0), C=(w,h), D=(0,h), so the rectangle area wh=70. Because AF=FG=GB, F=(w/3,0), G=(2w/3,0). Because E is the midpoint of DC, E=(w/2,h). The equation of diagonal AC is y=(h/w)x. Find H: EF can be parameterized as E+t(F-E), that is, (x,y)=(w/2-tw/6, h-th). When it intersects AC, h(1-t)=h(1/2-t/6), so 1-t=1/2-t/6, solving gives t=3/5. Therefore H=(2w/5,2h/5). Find J: EG can be parameterized as E+s(G-E), that is, (x,y)=(w/2+sw/6, h-sh). When it intersects AC, h(1-s)=h(1/2+s/6), so 1-s=1/2+s/6, solving gives s=3/7. method.method_draft: Use analytic coordinates. From the text, set the rectangle as A=(0,0), B=(w,0), C=(w,h), D=(0,h), with wh=70. Since AF=FG=GB, read F=(w/3,0) and G=(2w/3,0); since E is the midpoint of DC, E=(w/2,h). The image/text give that H is EF ∩ AC and J is EG ∩ AC. Write AC as y=(h/w)x. Parametrize EF by E+t(F−E), solve its intersection with AC to get H=(2w/5,2h/5). Parametrize EG by E+s(G−E), solve its intersection with AC to get J=(4w/7,4h/7). Then compute the area of triangle EHJ using the determinant formula: area = (1/2)|det(H−E,J−E)| = (3/70)wh = 3.
